Chapter 10: Spreading Sticky Ideas—From Individual Messages to Cultural Change.
So, what happens when a great idea isn’t just memorable for one person, but actually catches on and starts to shape entire groups—or even whole cultures? That’s where the magic of sticky ideas truly comes to life. When an idea really sticks, it’s more than just a catchy message. It becomes part of our collective memory—guiding the way people act and make decisions, sometimes for years to come.
Think about how these ideas travel. They don’t move on their own—they spread through social networks. When people hear a story that’s simple, concrete, and hits them emotionally, they can’t help but share it. Maybe it made them laugh, or maybe it tugged at their heart. Either way, it’s easy to retell, and suddenly, everyone’s talking about it. Now, if you’re a leader or a change-maker, you can help this along. How? By creating spaces where sharing and storytelling just happen naturally. Picture an organization where employees who live out the company’s values are recognized, and their stories become legends—stories that inspire everyone else to follow suit. So, how do you get your sticky idea out there? Here are a few simple ways:
First, empower your messengers. Encourage people at every level to share their own stories and examples. Next, create rituals and symbols. Use clear actions and memorable images to drive the message home. And finally, celebrate success. Shine a light on real-life moments when the idea is put into action.
Let’s make it real. Imagine a school hoping to build a culture of kindness. They could share stories of students helping each other, set up a “kindness wall” filled with good deeds, and publicly celebrate acts of generosity. Before long, kindness isn’t just a nice idea—it’s part of everyday life.
Over time, these sticky ideas can do more than shift what one person does. They can transform entire communities. When you keep the SUCCESs principles in mind and use them consistently, you’re not just sharing an idea. You’re planting seeds that can grow into real, lasting change.
